title: Checkpoint unpack scratchpad — partial tar + safetensors oddities
content:
Purpose: quick running log + hypotheses for the model-x v1 loading flake seen intermittently when spinning up Dedicated test nodes. Goal is to capture commands tried, errors observed, and next experiments so I can hand off to SRE/Storage if needed.

Observed symptom summary:
- Node pulls checkpoint tar from GCS and starts untar; sometimes tar aborts with 'Unexpected EOF' or 'tar: corrupt file header' when extracting a weights shard.
- When tar extraction fails, subsequent attempted partial downloads report correct size but unpack still errors.
- When extraction succeeds, downstream safetensors load sometimes throws header/shape mismatch on a single shard and model crashes during init.
- Failures not correlated to machine type so far; reproducible ~1/6 runs.

Timebox 2026-02-12 -> 2026-03-10: interactive debug transcript

2026-02-12 09:04 Blake - first reproducer\$ gsutil -m cp gs://redwood-checkpoints/model-x/v1/checkpoint.tar.gz /tmp/ckpt.tar.gz
Copy: gs://redwood-checkpoints/model-x/v1/checkpoint.tar.gz [Content-Length: 45872123456] -> /tmp/ckpt.tar.gz
(succeeds)
\$ tar -tzf /tmp/ckpt.tar.gz | head -n 20
weights/shard-0000.safetensors
weights/shard-0001.safetensors
metadata/manifest.json
...
\$ tar -xzf /tmp/ckpt.tar.gz -C /mnt/model || true
// intermittent error printed: 'tar: Unexpected EOF in archive'
// exit code 2 on some runs, sometimes 0

2026-02-14 14:20 Blake - tried resumable curl\$ curl -C - -o /tmp/ckpt.tar.gz 'https://storage.googleapis.com/redwood-checkpoints/model-x/v1/checkpoint.tar.gz'
[...progress...]
// completed file size matches Content-Length (45872123456 bytes)
\$ sha256sum /tmp/ckpt.tar.gz
// matches last-known sha in manifest locally (verified)
\$ tar -xzf /tmp/ckpt.tar.gz -C /mnt/model
tar: weights/shard-0001.safetensors: Unexpected EOF
tar: Error is not recoverable: exiting now

Notes: checksum match but tar extraction failing on particular file. Suggests archive header/trailing bytes corrupted in stream vs local copy? odd.

2026-02-17 11:03 Blake - inspect tar integrity with python\$ python - <<'PY'
import tarfile\p='/tmp/ckpt.tar.gz'
with tarfile.open(p,'r:gz') as t:
    for m in t.getmembers():
        if 'shard-0001' in m.name:
            print('member size', m.size, 'offset', m.offset)
            break
PY
// python tarfile also raises EOFError when iterating members on failing archive.

2026-02-19 16:40 Blake - try streaming copy and unpack with tar piped\$ gsutil cat gs://redwood-checkpoints/model-x/v1/checkpoint.tar.gz | tar -xz -C /mnt/model
// tar reports EOF again intermittently, but different runs sometimes succeed

2026-02-21 09:12 Blake - try list of file sizes inside tar vs GCS object composition\$ gsutil stat gs://redwood-checkpoints/model-x/v1/checkpoint.tar.gz
    Hash (crc32c): .....
    Content-Length: 45872123456

// downloaded to two different datacenter regions, same size and crc32c

2026-02-25 13:30 Blake - hypothesis A: tar created with sparse files or PAX headers that our tar binary mishandles when streaming from GCS.
Experiment:
- Create local tar.gz from original extracted checkpoint and reupload to a test bucket 'gs://blake-debug/test-ckpt.tar.gz' using 'tar -czf'.
- Download and extract on target node (multiple)
Result: extraction stable and no EOF errors.
Conclusion: original tar might have been created by a different tool producing slightly different gzip headers or multi-part upload interactions.

2026-03-02 10:00 Blake - hypothesis B: object was uploaded via compose/parallel uploads and some ranges are fine for byte-range reads but streaming pipe can trigger a composition boundary that our tar can't handle; local cp of whole object passes cryptographic checks but streaming hits internal discontinuity.
Test: use curl with range requests to read header ranges across the composition boundary.
Commands tried:
\$ curl -I 'https://storage.googleapis.com/redwood-checkpoints/model-x/v1/checkpoint.tar.gz'
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Accept-Ranges: bytes
Content-Length: 45872123456

// Try reading first 1MB and last 1MB to validate gzip footer and header continuity
\$ curl -r 0-1048575 -o /tmp/ckpt.h1 'https://storage.googleapis.com/redwood-checkpoints/model-x/v1/checkpoint.tar.gz'
\$ curl -r 45871119200-45872123455 -o /tmp/ckpt.h2 'https://storage.googleapis.com/redwood-checkpoints/model-x/v1/checkpoint.tar.gz'
// inspect gzip magic and last 8 bytes for CRC/ISIZE

2026-03-04 15:22 Blake - safetensors loading oddity after successful untar\$ python - <<'PY'
from safetensors import safe_open
try:
    with safe_open('/mnt/model/weights/shard-0001.safetensors','rb') as f:
        print('keys', f.keys())
        meta = f.get_metadata()
        print('meta', meta)
except Exception as e:
    print('ERR', type(e).__name__, str(e))
PY
Output on failing run: ERR SafetensorError invalid magic header

Other run (successful): prints keys and metadata normally. So safetensors file itself sometimes appears truncated/corrupted on disk only for that shard.

2026-03-06 09:50 Blake - low-level bytes check on shard file size\$ ls -l /mnt/model/weights/shard-0001.safetensors
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 2304899328 Mar  6 09:49 shard-0001.safetensors
\$ python -c "print(open('/mnt/model/weights/shard-0001.safetensors','rb').read()[-16:])"
// returns garbage on bad run; on good run returns gzip-ish footer bytes expected by safetensors writer

Hypotheses summary:
1) Upload composition / multi-part / parallel upload produced an object that is valid for range reads but not for streaming decompress in some client variants.
2) GCS edge caching + nginx chunked transfer encoding causing mid-stream truncation under certain concurrent load.
3) Local transient disk IO error on target node during tar extract leading to corrupt file write (less likely because same issue appears across machines).
4) Race where tar -xz and container file system overlay (overlayfs) cause file visible before fully written to disk when tar extracts in background; rare but possible with certain flags.

What I tried that reduced failure rate:
- use gsutil cp to write full object to local disk before extracting (reduced failures but not eliminated)
- increase ulimit -n and ulimit -f on container (no effect)
- disabled concurrent unpack by adding single-threaded tar extraction (tar --blocking-factor=20) (slight improvement)

Next experiments to run (ordered):
- Recreate tar.gz using the same tar command the original pipeline used (ask pipeline owner) and re-upload; verify if problem reproduces. (Priya to help; see PR link).
- Try 'gsutil compose' metadata checks and use signed URL with 'Accept-Ranges' to test streaming vs whole-object reads.
- Write a small python script to read the object from GCS in streaming chunks and run gzip.decompress incremental to detect exact byte offset where decompression fails. Save failing offset to a small file and check object integrity via byte-range fetch.
- For safetensors: add a post-extract quick validator that opens each safetensors block with safe_open and fails early; if invalid, re-download whole object and extract to a fresh directory.
- Engage storage team: provide failing object name, crc32c, upload trace, and sample failing offsets if streaming debug script finds deterministic offset.

Notes to self before handing off:
- Keep a copy of both the 'good' and 'bad' /tmp copies (sha256 sums) and include on JIRA ticket.
- Avoid trying to run full loads on prod; use small test nodes.
- If storage team cannot reproduce, instrument an HTTP proxy locally to record raw bytes during streaming to capture any invisible composition boundary behavior.

Snippets to repro incremental decompression offset detection (local debug):
python - <<'PY'
import requests, gzip
url='https://storage.googleapis.com/redwood-checkpoints/model-x/v1/checkpoint.tar.gz'
r=requests.get(url, stream=True)
obj=gzip.decompressobj()
offset=0
for chunk in r.iter_content(65536):
    try:
        obj.decompress(chunk)
    except Exception as e:
        print('decompress failed at offset', offset)
        open('/tmp/failing-offset.txt','w').write(str(offset))
        break
    offset += len(chunk)
PY

If this reliably finds an offset, then we can ask GCS to show compose boundaries or reassemble object.

Open questions:
- Which uploader produced the original file and does it use 'gsutil cp' vs parallel compose? Check upload job logs in artifact pipeline.
- Does our CI/CD pipeline do any on-the-fly recompression or metadata mutation?
- Is the safetensors writer being run by an older library version with different footer format? (check writer version in manifest)

Hand-off checklist for storage/SRE:
- Provide object name, crc32c, content-length, sha256 of full object (both good and bad copies), and failing offsets if available.
- Ask storage to run server-side integrity check and list any compose operations for that object.
- If server claims object is fine, instrument HTTP edge to dump raw bytes for a failing extraction attempt.

Small TODOs:
- [ ] Implement streaming offset detector and run 10x across random nodes (Blake)
- [ ] Ask Priya for pipeline upload command and re-create bundle (Priya)
- [ ] Attach reproducible failing tar and good tar to JIRA INF-1293 (Blake)
- [ ] Add safetensors quick-validate to extraction path as temporary mitigation (Riley)

End of scratchpad.
